business: Clockout (Donovin Sims, Roscoe IL) — business optimization and AI implementation for owner-led local businesses
target: owner-led service businesses in northern Illinois with roughly 2-25 employees, where the owner still answers the phone, quotes the work and personally decides what to buy

segments.name: Owner of a 2-9 person trade or home-service business (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, cleaning, auto, restoration)
Owner of a 10-25 person service business (multi-crew trades, dental/medical office, retail, property services)
Independent operator or solo professional (single truck, solo agent, one-chair shop)
Small property manager or portfolio operator (40-200 units)

behaviours.name: Burned before by a marketing agency
behaviours.how: paid $500-$2,000 a month for a year, got reports about clicks and almost no jobs, and still resents it

behaviours.name: Price-first deal hunter
behaviours.how: asks 'how much' in the first two minutes and compares every quote to the cheapest number on the table

behaviours.name: Referral-only buyer
behaviours.how: buys almost nothing cold; wants to know who else in town used this person and how it went

behaviours.name: Do-it-myself owner
behaviours.how: built the current website or set up the software himself at 11pm and is quietly proud and quietly exhausted by it

behaviours.name: Software collector
behaviours.how: already pays for a CRM, a scheduling app and a review tool, uses about a third of each, and suspects the answer is not another subscription

behaviours.name: AI skeptic
behaviours.how: has read the hype, thinks most of it is a chatbot, and worries a robot will answer a customer wrong and cost him the job

behaviours.name: Fast decider when trust is there
behaviours.how: if the person seems straight and the price is clear, he decides in one meeting and hates being sold to twice

objections: I got burned by a marketing agency before and I'm not doing that again
I don't have time to sit in meetings about this
AI sounds like hype, and I can't have a robot saying the wrong thing to my customers
How do I know this will actually pay for itself?
I already pay for software I barely use
That's real money for something I can't see yet
I don't want another monthly contract I can't get out of
My business is different — a guy from outside the trade won't get it
habits: reads email on his phone in the truck between jobs, thumbs only
Monday morning is invoices, payroll and paperwork he has been putting off
either answers the phone in the middle of a job or misses it entirely
quotes by text or on a paper pad, then forgets to follow up on half of them
talks to two other owners a week, usually at the supply house or on a ball field
does the books at the kitchen table on Sunday night
